replicates.rationale: Both reject on-the-spot receptor design and state pre-existing diversity, selection, proliferation, and preserved B-cell/antibody specificity. B is slightly more compact, but neither has a material conceptual advantage.

Both clearly explain pre-existing receptors, selection, and expansion, and both avoid antigen-as-designer. Neither directly states that descendants preserve the same specificity. B gives the same model with lower reading cost and a compact process summary.

Both resolve the main confusion and avoid saying antigen designs receptors. A better preserves the specificity boundary by saying the copied cells are same or similar and by tying B-cell receptor and secreted antibody to the same recognition structure. B is a bit leaner, but misses descendants preserving specificity.

item_observation: Strong answers should center clonal selection: receptor diversity is generated before exposure; antigen selects an already matching clone; activation expands it; descendants retain antigen specificity. The key forbidden move is implying the virus instructs receptor design.
